editorial:
The Ape (1940) is a Monogram Pictures horror film with Boris Karloff. The Internet Archive item the_ape runs 1:02:23 in black and white. Creators want it as a Karloff vehicle that is cheap to clip, riff on or screen.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not settled. A 1940 film is free only if it lacked a copyright notice or its renewal was missed. The renewal window is 1968, with 1967 and 1969 as adjacent years, and those years are checked in the Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes. No renewal has been confirmed or ruled out, because no verified line-by-line read has been done. The source play is a second layer whose term was not checked. Treat the film as unconfirmed until both are checked.
faq: Is The Ape (1940) public domain in the US?

Not confirmed. It is a 1940 film, so it is free only if its copyright notice was missing or it was never renewed. The renewal window is 1968, with 1967 and 1969 as adjacent years. Those years need a line-by-line check of the Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes. The Copyright Office online catalog is only a secondary check, because it covers records from 1978 onward. Copies exist on the Internet Archive, and its item pages show a Public Domain label. That label is the uploader's, not proof of status.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies of The Ape?

The Internet Archive's public-domain label is not proof of status. Do your own renewal check first. Also check the play it was adapted from, and any added material in a particular upload. The two uploads run 1:02:23 and 57:28, so the shorter one may be an edited print.
